A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Prism Hypothesis and Unified Autoencoding study. All 11 pages of each are readable, including equations, figures, tables and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original spectral analyses, retrieval experiments, UAE reconstruction and generation results, linear probing, and ablations in Figures 2–6 and Tables 1–6.

after.justification: v2 retains the original spectral analyses, retrieval experiments, UAE evaluations and ablations reported in v1.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same DINOv2-based encoder, FFT band decomposition, residual splitting, noise injection, spectral transform, semantic loss and three-stage training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ImageNet-1K and MS-COCO 2017 reconstruction, ImageNet generation and classification, and the same spectral and retrieval scenarios. Table 1's added 'full set' wording does not establish newly evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain identical comparator membership for reconstruction, generation and linear probing. The methods compared in the figures also remain unchanged; citation renumbering does not introduce different baselines.

E3.justification: The stated resolutions, metrics, model sizes, training stages and 30-epoch linear-probing protocol remain unchanged. Table 1 newly describes the evaluation as 'full set', but v1 specified no conflicting subset; this is additional documentation rather than an established protocol revision.

E4.justification: Tables 4–6 retain the same module ablations, band-count sweep and semantic comparisons. The frequency-energy analysis, filtering robustness experiment, reconstruction examples and t-SNE analysis are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–6 and the plotted and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, UAE retains generation gFID 1.68 and IS 301.6 in Table 2, and 83.0% linear-probing accuracy in Table 3.

T1.justification: The spectral-filtering definitions, formalized hypothesis conditions and Equations (1)–(7) are unchanged. No theorem, proof or mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same Prism Hypothesis, unified-representation claims and performance claims. Changed citations do not alter their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning low-frequency semantics, high-frequency detail, reconstruction quality and robustness to band granularity remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added or removed.

D1.justification: Table 1's caption adds 'full set' to the ImageNet-1K/MS-COCO 2017 evaluation description. This supplies a limited evaluation detail without specifying sample counts or establishing a changed experiment. Other implementation details and the repository link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction replaces Dosovitskiy et al.'s ViT reference with Nguyen et al.'s individual-pixel transformer paper. The NVG bibliography entry is removed, although its discussion survives with an unresolved '[?]' citation. The substantive positioning otherwise remains unchanged; most other reference edits concern metadata.

P1.justification: Bibliographic entries receive widespread author, title, venue and page-detail edits, with accompanying citation renumbering. The version/date stamp and a short caption phrase also change. Main-text wording and section organization otherwise remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1's caption changes and the bibliography reflows. v2 also introduces a black rectangle covering Table 2's 'Methods' header. Figure content, table structures and their placement otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The 'full set' clarification and fuller bibliographic details improve documentation, but v2 also loses the resolvable NVG reference and obscures Table 2's header. With the scientific content and evidence unchanged, these competing documentation gains and attribution/layout defects leave the net quality effect unclear.
